title: Postgres execute_select_query pastes raw clauses into SQL; read-only is only a keyword blocklist
reason: Every clause argument is interpolated into the SQL text and the only 'SELECT only' guard checks the first word of select_clause, so an injected caller can read any table/schema the connection user can (e.g. pg_shadow, other tenants' rows), run data-modifying CTEs in with_clause and call side-effect functions (pg_terminate_backend, pg_read_file, dblink) with the connection's privileges.
fix: Connect with a dedicated read-only role limited to the intended schemas and run each query in a READ ONLY transaction (SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY) with a statement_timeout; validate identifiers against the discovered table list instead of a keyword blocklist.

title: ClickHouse query tools interpolate raw clauses and identifiers with no readonly setting
reason: from_clause/table_name go straight into the query and the client is created without readonly settings, so a caller can read every database the user can and use ClickHouse table functions such as url('http://169.254.169.254/...') or file()/remote() to make the DB server fetch internal URLs or files (subject to server settings).
fix: Create the client with settings={'readonly': 1} and a DB user without URL/file/remote table-function grants; check database/table names against the discovered list and quote them with backticks.

title: MongoDB aggregate tool uses a blocklist that misses server-side JavaScript
reason: Only $out/$merge/$where and update operators are blocked; $function/$accumulator (server-side JS) and $lookup/$unionWith into any collection pass, and database_name is caller-chosen, so the tool can read any database the connection user can and run JS on the server.
fix: Use a MongoDB user with the read role on the intended database only, disable server-side scripting (security.javascriptEnabled: false), and allowlist pipeline stages/operators instead of blocklisting.

title: /mcp HTTP endpoint has no authentication and no Origin/Host check
reason: Unlike /worker/* (JWT), /mcp accepts any caller and request header validation only checks the session id, so anything that can reach the port (other users on a 0.0.0.0 bind, or a web page via DNS rebinding against 127.0.0.1) can call every tool with the server's configured secrets and OAuth tokens.
fix: Require authentication on /mcp (bearer token or the same worker JWT), validate Origin and Host against an allowlist (localhost only by default), and refuse to bind to non-loopback addresses without auth configured.

title: Worker secret written to logs on every bad JWT

evidence.quote: "Invalid signature. Is the Arcade Engine configured with the Worker secret '%s'?",

reason: Any unauthenticated request with a badly signed JWT makes the server log the HS256 worker secret in clear text; whoever can read logs can then mint valid worker tokens and call tools.
fix: Remove the secret from the log message (log only that the signature was invalid); rotate any worker secret that has appeared in logs.

title: docker-compose publishes Redis on all interfaces with an empty password
reason: Following the example config exposes an unauthenticated Redis (used by the engine) on every host interface, letting anyone on the network read or alter its data.
fix: Do not publish 6379 (keep Redis on the internal network) or bind it to 127.0.0.1, and set a strong REDIS_PASSWORD.

title: Example env ships guessable worker/root secrets
reason: These are placeholders, not leaked keys, but a deployment that copies env.example to .env gets a worker secret of 'dev', which lets anyone forge worker JWTs.
fix: Leave the values empty in env.example and make the server refuse to start with a known default secret.

title: Bright Data scrape returns arbitrary web pages raw to the model
reason: Scraped page markdown goes into the model context unmarked; when this toolkit is served together with the GitHub/Slack/DB toolkits, text on a page can steer the model to read private data and send it out.
fix: Mark scraped content as untrusted data in the result and avoid serving web-scraping tools in the same server as write/send tools without client approval.

title: Generated API wrappers put path arguments into URLs without encoding

evidence.quote: file_path: Annotated[str, "The file path in the repository to be deleted. This path is case-sensitive."],

reason: Values like `../../user/keys` or ones containing `?`/`#` change which endpoint on the same API host is called with the user's token; the host itself is fixed by operator secrets, so the impact is limited to the token's scopes.
fix: URL-encode each path parameter in the generator (urllib.parse.quote(value, safe='')) and reject values containing '/' unless the parameter is meant to be a path.

title: Destructive wrapper tools have no confirmation step
reason: Tools such as delete_github_repository (and similar delete/send/pay tools across the generated toolkits) act immediately; whether a human approves them depends on the MCP client, which is not in this repo.
fix: Mark destructive tools (MCP destructiveHint annotation) and require client-side approval or an explicit confirm parameter; ship only the toolkits a deployment needs.
